title: The 3.8.0 med defects are fixed: locks, guard false positive, the affected listing, dependants at mint, and the empty task gate
description: D9: a med defect holds a release. Register entries F754, F800, F809 (open part), F792 (with its P151 recurrences) and F779, each verified open against main on 2026-10-29/31, plus F821's release-tier flake in tests/test__locks.py.
desiredOutcome: Each entry's Do is met with a case that goes red on the defect, the register status of each reads FIXED with its commit, and release-tier CI is green on the phase's landing commit.

tasks.title: A phase lock held by the caller's own process under an earlier session id is reported as the caller's, and a dead drive's lock is not read as a live run
tasks.description: Register F754. When a Claude Code conversation continues under a new session id in the same process, the phase lock taken under the old id reads as HELD by a live run forever (the holder pid is the long-lived claude process), and only release --session <old> --pid <pid> lets go. Do: when the caller's process ancestry contains the holder pid but the session differs, say so and offer the release by name; and base liveness on the drive command's own pid or a heartbeat rather than the long-lived claude process, so a dead drive releases. A lock held by an unrelated live pid still refuses.

add: tests/test__locks.py: a lock held by an ancestor pid under another session id is reported as the caller's own with the release offered by name; a lock held by an unrelated live pid still refuses

outcome.technical:
plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_locks.py: new _parent_of (self via os.getppid, /proc//stat, `ps -o ppid=`, Toolhelp32 snapshot on Windows), _ancestry (nearest first, excludes self and pid 1, stops on repeat, limit 64), _own_earlier_session (hand-off claim only; not a claim recording a takeover from the caller via taken_from; claim session present and different from the caller's; same host; recorded pid in the caller's ancestry), _own_release_lines (prints the whole `audit-lock.py release --project

--session --pid `, shlex-quoted, shlex imported lazily since hooks resolve this module on every tool call). acquire's E_LIVE refusal and release's mismatch refusal both use it: the exit code stays E_LIVE and the claim is never adopted, only named and offered. Module docstring gains one paragraph; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's _locks section gains the matching sentence. tests/test__locks.py: new ap-block (_ancestor_cases) with ap1, ap1b, ap1c, ap1d, ap1e, ap2, ap2b, ap2c, ap3; wt3 not touched. Runs: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__locks.py` exit 0, 147 cases. Dependant sweep `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__locks.py tests/test_audit_lock.py tests/test__output_lints.py tests/test__deps.py tests/test_drive_phase.py tests/test__invariants.py tests/test_stamp_verification.py tests/test_audit_task.py` exit 0 (8/8 files ok, 3007 cases); a second sweep over test__evidence_io, test__proc_group, test__status_facts, test__refs, test__proposals, test_merge_manifest also exit 0. test__deps and test__output_lints re-run after the final guide edit: 254/254 and 173/173. ruff and vermin -t=3.8- on both .py files exit 0. NOT DONE, for the reviewer to decide: the Do's second half (liveness of a hand-off claim based on the drive command's own pid or a heartbeat). The drive exits after every step while its lock is kept on purpose (drive-phase.py drive(): the lock is kept while a decision is pending or a dispatch is out), so the drive's pid would read gone between steps, and audit-task.py _take_phase_lock takes over a lock whose holder_gone is true, so a second session would seize a phase whose executor is still running. A heartbeat window brings back the age rule that audit-lock.py's WHY LIVENESS, NOT AGE section rejects: a human-confirmation pause holds the lock with no command running, so it would read stale. Both would need drive-phase.py or audit-lock.py (not declared), plus an owner decision. Dependants: _evidence_io, _invariants, _proc_group, stamp-verification, _proposals, merge-manifest are unchanged (they read codes, held_by_us or pid_alive, and none of those changed). audit-lock.py now prints the new wording only for an ancestor's hand-off claim under another session (its sl3 shows it, still green). audit-task.py (_take_phase_lock reads E_LIVE as held, unchanged; test_audit_task k1b checks the generic wording, which is kept because its caller names no session). Names _age_minutes, _claim_stamp, _displaced_record, _identity are unchanged. test__locks.py dependants: .github/sweep-costs.json (no stage table here; the new block adds a few seconds and is not re-recorded), tools/verify.sh (path only). PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md dependants: test__deps enumeration lint green, and the others name it by basename only. Plan gate refusal for the probe in the worktree, verbatim except the checkout path written as /...: '[require-plan] probe/mutations.py is outside task P153.1, the task this worktree is bound to (plan: /dev/audit-plugin/claude-plugins): no task of this plan declares it for this one. Only that task's files are open here.' So the probe sits at /probe/mutations.py (takes TREE as its argument; output in /probe/output.txt). It was run against an rsync copy of the worktree, never the worktree itself, and exited 0: 7 KILLED (never names the ancestor -> ap1/ap1c/ap1e; ancestry ignored -> ap2; handedOff gate dropped -> ap2b; taken_from gate dropped -> ap2c + test_audit_lock c7b; release keeps old wording -> ap1e; walk stops at parent -> ap3; offer drops --pid -> ap1/ap1c/ap1e), RESTORED tree green.
outcome.descriptive: A phase lock held by the caller's own process under an earlier session id is now named as the caller's own, with the exact release command printed, on both acquire and release. Unrelated live holders, a parent's own-write claim and a takeover still refuse as before. The heartbeat/drive-pid liveness half was not done; it needs a design decision.

verifiedBy: ap1: an ancestor's hand-off claim under an earlier session is reported as 'your own' with `release phase-P1 ... --session s-EARLIER --pid <ppid>` offered, exit E_LIVE, found through ancestry alone (pid argument is this process)
ap1b: the claim is left byte-identical (not adopted)
ap1c: same when the caller's pid argument equals the holder (the $CLAUDE_PID shape)
ap1d: the offered release actually lets the claim go
ap1e: release under the later session is refused with the same naming and offer and is not told it was taken over
ap2: an unrelated live pid (a child, not an ancestor) still refuses and gets no offer
ap2b: an ancestor's own-write (not handed off) claim refuses and gets no offer
ap2c: a claim recording a takeover from the caller, held by an ancestor pid, is still reported as a takeover on release
ap3: a child's ancestry walk lists this process and its parent, nearest first (the walk goes past one level)

tasks.title: wt3's stand-in holder lets go the way a real holder does, so a Windows sharing-denied unlink cannot leave the claim behind
tasks.description: Register F821. tests/test__locks.py wt3's timer deletes the claim once through _unlink_quietly (a swallowed os.unlink); on Windows that unlink is refused while the waiter has the claim open in read_lock, so the claim stays and the waiter refuses at the 5 s bound (release-tier run 41161967355 attempt 1, resample pass 3). Have the holder let go through M.release(...), the product path that retries the sharing denial via _output.while_shared, and add a row that injects one denied unlink: the old holder goes red, the fixed one green. Do not widen the margin. Probes: the session scratchpad f821/probe/wt3_forced.py.

tasks.title: guard-uncommitted reads a heredoc body or a quoted argument as data, not as a command, so a description that quotes git is not refused
tasks.description: Register F800. The guard refused an audit-task.py add whose heredoc description merely quoted git commands: it could not tokenize the command, assumed the widest loss set, and refused; the same description passed on stdin from a file. Bind the evidence to the operation: when the command cannot be tokenized, read only what is outside heredoc bodies and quoted arguments; red-first the allow case and keep the deny case red.

add: .claude/hooks/guard-uncommitted.py: an audit-task add whose heredoc description quotes a stash command and a checkout is allowed; the same commands run outside the heredoc are still refused

tasks.title: scope --gate-clear on a tdd or regression task refuses, or falls back to the phase gate, rather than closing the task with no gate
tasks.description: Register F779 (verified 2026-10-31 at ad838231): audit-task.py scope <task> --gate-clear on a tdd task exits 0 and writes {gate: [], gateBasis: cleared}; run-test-gate reports empty-gate. A task can close with no gate while the record reads green. Pick the structurally correct answer (refuse on tdd/regression, or fall back to the phase gate with the basis saying so) and check the drive's close path end to end.

add: tests/test_audit_task.py: scope --gate-clear on a tdd task neither writes an empty gate silently nor lets the task close as green

tasks.title: A task's related-suite listing keeps the hook and tool gates the affected selection names
tasks.description: Register F809, open part (verified 2026-10-31 at ad838231): _related_suite_paths throws away the gates select() names that are not tests/ suites, so "affected.py --list-related plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/_manifest_vocab.py" prints only tests/ while "affected.py --json" names guard-release.py and arm-release-bypass.py --selftest; a task gate does not run those hooks and the miss measurement (which counts --json gates) cannot see it. Keep scanners out (S3.3) but keep every non-scanner gate select() names.

add: tests/test__affected_tests.py: for plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/_manifest_vocab.py the task listing includes .claude/hooks/guard-release.py --selftest and arm-release-bypass.py --selftest, which affected.py --json names

tasks.title: A task that deletes, renames or changes a file other files read cannot be dispatched until each such dependant is declared or waived with a reason, and scope can add files without restating the held list
tasks.description: Register F792 (verified open 2026-10-31 at ad838231; recurred twice in P151 and three times in P143 as undeclared edits). The brief already lists "Who depends on this" (audit-lookup.dependant_lines) but only asks the executor to answer each dependant, and nothing grades it. Do: from the same dependants data, list at dispatch every tracked file that reads a declared file (by path, by import, or by text anchor, e.g. tools/prove-gates.py rows anchored on ci.yml and gate-parity.py text) that the task does not declare, and refuse dispatch until each is declared or waived with a recorded reason. Also let scope take an incremental +a,b spelling. Keep the refusal precise: a dependant that cannot be affected by the declared change shape must not be demanded (measure the false-positive rate over the last phases P143 and P151 and report it).

add: tests/test_audit_task.py: dispatch of a task whose declared change has an undeclared dependant is refused naming it, and passes once it is declared or waived with a reason; scope --files +a,b adds to the held list
